name: MonarchAiConversation
title: useAiConversation
wrapsNative: kotlinx.coroutines.flow.StateFlow over an injected transport that returns kotlinx.coroutines.flow.Flow, collected in a caller-supplied CoroutineScope
summary: Headless state for an AI conversation: it sends prompts through an injected transport, streams the reply into the vendor-neutral message model, and handles stop, regenerate, retry, edit and resend as branches, tool approval, client-side tools, an offline queue and feedback.
whenToUse: As the model behind any chat surface. Create it with rememberMonarchAiConversation, or in a ViewModel with viewModelScope, collect messages, status and error in the UI, and implement MonarchAiTransport for your backend.
whenNotToUse: It draws nothing: use the AI components (MonarchAiArtifactCard, MonarchAiErrorMessage and the others) to show the messages. For a single completion in a text field, call your service directly.
api: class MonarchAiConversation(transport: MonarchAiTransport, scope: CoroutineScope, connectionLostMessage: String, toolResultFailedMessage: String, initialMessages: List<MonarchAiConversationMessage> = emptyList(), conversationId: String? = null, body: Map<String, MonarchAiJSON> = emptyMap(), queuesWhileOffline: Boolean = true, slowAfterMillis: Long? = 10_000L, generateId: (() -> String)? = null)

val messages: StateFlow<List<MonarchAiConversationMessage>>; val status: StateFlow<MonarchAiConversationStatus>; val error: StateFlow<MonarchAiConversationError?>; val conversationId: StateFlow<String?>; val agent: StateFlow<MonarchAiAgentRef?>; val slow: StateFlow<Boolean>; val online: StateFlow<Boolean>; val queued: StateFlow<List<MonarchAiQueuedMessage>>; val busy: Boolean; val canSend: Boolean

var body: Map<String, MonarchAiJSON>; var onFinish: ((MonarchAiConversationMessage) -> Unit)?; var onError: ((MonarchAiConversationError) -> Unit)?; var onToolResponse: ((MonarchAiToolResponse) -> Unit)?; var onToolCall: (suspend (MonarchAiToolCallPart) -> MonarchAiJSON)?; var toolPolicy: ((MonarchAiToolCallPart) -> MonarchAiToolDecision)?; var onMemoryEvent: ((MonarchAiMemoryPart, MonarchAiConversationMessage) -> Unit)?
fun send(text: String, files: List<MonarchAiFilePart> = emptyList(), body: Map<String, MonarchAiJSON> = emptyMap()): Boolean

fun cancelQueued(id: String); fun setOnline(online: Boolean); fun stop(); fun regenerate(messageId: String? = null, body: Map<String, MonarchAiJSON> = emptyMap()); fun retry(messageId: String? = null, body: Map<String, MonarchAiJSON> = emptyMap()); fun editAndResend(messageId: String, text: String, files: List<MonarchAiFilePart>? = null, body: Map<String, MonarchAiJSON> = emptyMap())

fun approveTool(toolCallId: String, input: MonarchAiJSON? = null); fun denyTool(toolCallId: String, reason: String? = null); fun submitToolResult(toolCallId: String, result: MonarchAiToolResult); fun resumeRun(messageId: String? = null); fun branchTo(messageId: String, index: Int); fun setFeedback(messageId: String, feedback: MonarchAiMessageFeedback?); fun reset(messages: List<MonarchAiConversationMessage> = emptyList())

@Composable fun rememberMonarchAiConversation(transport: MonarchAiTransport, initialMessages: List<MonarchAiConversationMessage> = emptyList(), conversationId: String? = null, queuesWhileOffline: Boolean = true, slowAfterMillis: Long? = 10_000L, connectionLostMessage: String? = null, toolResultFailedMessage: String? = null): MonarchAiConversation

interface MonarchAiTransport { fun stream(request: MonarchAiTransportRequest): Flow<MonarchAiStreamEvent>; val respondsToTools: Boolean; fun respondToTool(response: MonarchAiToolResponse): Flow<MonarchAiStreamEvent>; val resumesRuns: Boolean; fun resume(request: MonarchAiResumeRequest): Flow<MonarchAiStreamEvent> }
sealed interface MonarchAiStreamEvent { Agent, TextDelta, ReasoningDelta, ReasoningEnd, Part, ToolUpdate, ToolInputDelta, Finish, Run, Usage, Memory, Done, Error }

data class MonarchAiConversationMessage(id, role, parts, createdAt, agent, model, usage, feedback, branch, finishReason, runId, queued) { val text: String; val streaming: Boolean; val toolCalls; val memories; val createdAtMillis: Long?; fun toJson(): MonarchAiJSON; companion object { fun fromJson(json: MonarchAiJSON); fun listFromJson(text: String); fun listToJson(messages): String; fun timestamp(millis: Long): String } }

sealed interface MonarchAiPart { val type: String } implemented by MonarchAiTextPart, MonarchAiReasoningPart, MonarchAiToolCallPart, MonarchAiCitationPart, MonarchAiSourcePart, MonarchAiFilePart, MonarchAiArtifactPart, MonarchAiEditProposalPart, MonarchAiPlanPart, MonarchAiUiPart, MonarchAiMemoryPart, MonarchAiErrorPart
Value types: MonarchAiPlanStep, MonarchAiUsage, MonarchAiAgentRef, MonarchAiBranchPosition, MonarchAiJSON (Null, Bool, Number, Text, Array, Object; parse, toJsonString)

Enumerations: MonarchAiRole, MonarchAiPartState, MonarchAiToolCallState, MonarchAiToolCallRisk, MonarchAiFinishReason, MonarchAiSourceKind, MonarchAiArtifactKind, MonarchAiEditProposalState, MonarchAiPlanStepState, MonarchAiMemoryAction, MonarchAiMessageFeedback, MonarchAiTrigger, MonarchAiConversationStatus, MonarchAiToolDecision

Requests and results: MonarchAiTransportRequest, MonarchAiToolResponse, MonarchAiResumeRequest, MonarchAiToolCallPatch, MonarchAiQueuedMessage, MonarchAiToolResult (Output, Failure), MonarchAiConversationError (companion fun isRetryable(code: String?): Boolean)

options.name: transport
options.description: Connects the conversation to your backend. Monarch does no networking.

options.name: scope
options.description: Collects replies and runs client-side tools. Use a main-thread scope such as viewModelScope; rememberMonarchAiConversation uses rememberCoroutineScope().

options.name: connectionLostMessage
options.description: The message of the error raised when the transport's flow throws. Built-in: monarch_aiconversation_connection_lost.

options.name: toolResultFailedMessage
options.description: The error of a client-side tool that threw without a message. Built-in: monarch_aiconversation_tool_result_failed.

options.name: initialMessages
options.description: Messages to start with, for example a stored conversation. Shown as one branch.

options.name: conversationId
options.description: The id from an earlier session, sent with every request. A Done event replaces it.

options.name: body
options.description: Request fields sent on every turn, merged under the fields given to send. Also a settable property.

options.name: queuesWhileOffline
options.description: While offline, send keeps the message in queued and sends it, in order, once setOnline(true) is called.

options.name: slowAfterMillis
options.description: The time without any event from a running reply before slow becomes true. null turns it off.

options.name: generateId
options.description: Custom message ids. The default is a random UUID.

states.name: Submitted
states.description: Sent, waiting for the first event. busy is true.

states.name: Streaming
states.description: Events are arriving and messages changes with each one. busy is true.

states.name: AwaitingApproval
states.description: A tool call waits for approveTool or denyTool. canSend is false and send returns false.

states.name: AwaitingToolResult
states.description: The model called a tool the client runs: onToolCall runs it, or call submitToolResult.

states.name: Error
states.description: The last turn failed. error holds the code, the message and whether it can be retried or resumed; the reply ends with an error part.

states.name: Stopped
states.description: stop() ended the reply. What arrived stays, streaming parts are closed and running tool calls are cancelled.

states.name: offline
states.description: After setOnline(false), sent messages wait in queued and appear at the end of messages with queued set.

states.name: slow
states.description: slow is true while a running reply has sent nothing for slowAfterMillis.

appearance: None: it is a model and draws nothing.
platformNotes: The web is the useAiConversation hook; Android has a class with StateFlows, created with rememberMonarchAiConversation or in a ViewModel. The message model has the web's fields and reads and writes the web's JSON (camelCase fields, kebab-case values, a type field per part, empty optional fields left out), with a small built-in JSON reader so no serialisation library is added. Kotlin names follow Android: booleans without is (queued, redacted, retryable, resumable, approved, streaming, busy, online, slow), times in milliseconds (durationMs, retryAfterMs, slowAfterMillis), and createdAtMillis next to the ISO 8601 createdAt. Parts are a sealed interface the part classes implement, where iOS wraps them in enum cases. The transport returns a Flow; there is no AbortSignal: stopping cancels the collection. Not offered, because they belong to the browser or to a transport: file uploads (send takes file parts the app has already uploaded), the SSE, provider, AG-UI and Rook transports and their mappers, and the testing kit. The Rook transport stays Rook-scoped. The network state comes from setOnline, fed by the app, for example from a ConnectivityManager callback. The slow timer restarts on every event. With a tool policy, every waiting call is put to the policy before the status is decided, as on iOS.
accessibility: It draws nothing and announces nothing; the components that show the messages do.
slow, queued, the error message and the tool call states are plain values, so a view can show and announce them.
edgeCases: Sending while a reply streams ends that reply, keeping what arrived, and starts the next.
A Done or Error event ends the reply even if the transport keeps the flow open; a flow that ends without Done leaves the status Idle and does not call onFinish.
A flow that throws ends the reply with the retryable code network. With a run id and a transport that resumes runs, the error is resumable.
retry rewrites the same message; regenerate and editAndResend add a branch, and messages then carry branch with the index and count.
A queued message that fails holds the rest of the queue until the connection comes back again.
Sending a new message cancels tool calls that still waited for a client-side result.
Ending the scope cancels the collection of the transport's flow and any client-side tools.
Reading a part with an unknown type throws IllegalArgumentException.
The functions are not thread-safe: call them from the thread of the scope, normally the main thread.
